windows_reviewed_images.review: Real coastline dominates the Day view; DEMO and persistent AIS alert are unmistakable. Numeric rail is legible. With the alert visible the lower heading card requires the provided rail scroll controls.
Primary chrome, data rail and software coastline use the dim Night palette; alarm remains visible. Lower rail content still requires scrolling.
Destination, next point, remaining distance, advisory passage time and rounded arrival SOC are clear; synthetic route provenance is explicit.

Battery, propulsion and destination cards are legible; motor power differs from whole-pack consumption; ETA, reserve and estimated quality are explicit. Range content continues in the scroll viewport.

Correct Beta version, exact commit, MSVC, upstream, DPI, source ages and model provenance are visible. Minor retained caption says ALPHA 1 / NOT FOR NAVIGATION; this cosmetic wording is recorded as a Beta limitation, not a build identity ambiguity.
All retained energy inputs are grey with STALE ages; arrival, range, route distance and ETA are unavailable with Battery SOC stale reason. Alert strip stays above the page.
Normal OpenCPN Legacy toolbar/menu and real coastline are present.
Safe title and original OpenCPN chart/controls visible with real coastline; no XNav product panel.
Legacy to XNav returns with real coastline intact; Demo stops and missing live values remain unavailable.
Safe to XNav retains coastline and isolated profile; no fabricated navigation after restart.
Real OpenCPN loopback acquisition shows 68 percent SOC, 343 V, 820 RPM and forward gear; unconfigured identity/current/model and absent route suppress estimates.
Underlying sensor expiry removes battery/motor observations and forecasts while still-live discrete gear/regen remain separately sourced; warning is above the page.

Configured boat mapping shows SOC 68, 343 V, 21 A, 820 RPM, motor 62 C and regeneration Two bars. V times I is labelled estimated whole-pack power; no active route/GPS means no fabricated arrival/range.

Actual OpenCPN TCP loopback panel reports subsequent-feedback confirmation, locked/actual magnetic heading 328 and unavailable rudder. TRACK/WIND are visibly unavailable; this is software loopback evidence only.
Persistent critical feedback-loss alarm and TimedOut/outcome-unknown/no-retry text are visible; retained heading values are grey. Last AUTO label is explicitly qualified by stale feedback.
Reconnected STANDBY feedback is current while control is disabled; locked heading remains unavailable and actual magnetic heading is separately live.
Commissioning actions, OFF-at-start recording state, retention/privacy information and separate replay controls are readable; alert/navigation access remains present.
REPLAY is conspicuous in status and page; historical observations and disabled controls are explicit. Instruments-only recording supplies no fabricated active route or arrival.
Calibration export action and bench source/age rows remain accessible after scrolling. Actual CSV validation is recorded separately by the runtime harness.
Explicit diagnostic ZIP success, no-upload statement, privacy exclusions and optional selected-recording controls are readable; global alert remains visible.
At 125 percent, Night chrome and coastline remain dim and the main chart remains dominant. Lower COG/heading rail entries require scrolling.
At 150 percent the menu's final Field diagnostic bundle action is fully visible and the endpoint remains stable; the former focus jump is absent.
Night pilot page is consistently styled at 150 percent, with explicit DEMO/control-disabled state. Expanded controls require scrolling; fixed bottom Pilot/STBY access remains present.
Actual native sheet uses the Night palette; capacity field and Cancel/Save plus scroll controls fit without resizing the dialog.
At 150 percent cards keep readable full-size values and scroll instead of shrinking. Destination and lower card details require Down; fixed navigation and alert remain visible.

All System actions fit on-screen at 150 percent. The popup partly overlaps the right Alerts button, while the critical text at left stays visible; dismiss the transient popup before opening Alerts. Recorded as a manual-test presentation limitation.
Native 1920 by 1080 fullscreen at 144 DPI has intact display controls, alert and navigation, with no OS title bar. This capture is not a 1280 by 800 fullscreen claim.
At 150 percent Legacy return retains real coastline and explicit unavailable data; lower rail values use the scroll controls.
Actual loopback AIS card shows upstream SOG/COG/heading, bearing/range, CPA 0.4 NM and TCPA 7.5 min with age/estimated labels and upstream alarm. Chart selection is available.
Selected upstream AIS target is centered and visibly bracketed on the real chart; no independent collision interpretation.

Real coastline and selected live navigation rail remain unobscured during the route harness. This particular capture says Route unavailable; the 26 structured route-state checks, not its filename, establish active-route distance behavior.
Native manager is fully painted with Dashboard, GRIB and WMM enabled and Ok/Cancel/Apply controls. Advanced native dialog styling is deliberately preserved.
Native returned XNav retains real NOAA ENC soundings, shoreline, chart labels, route line and live vessel; no blank/all-water restart regression.
Native Beta 1 Setup completion page correctly identifies installed Beta 1 and offers optional launch; no error dialog.
Installed XNav after mode round-trip retains coastline/background chart; absent live sensors explicitly unavailable.
Restored original OpenCPN 5.12.4 Legacy executable renders coastline and native tools after uninstall; preservation verified separately by hashes.

After three actual hours, DEMO and critical AIS alert remain explicit; coastline, live wind/depth/speed/course, route summary and bottom actions remain visible. Heading needs rail scrolling when alert occupies height; no blank chart.
Dark Anchor watch surface distinguishes unavailable anchor/radius from live DEMO vessel, SOC/depth; historical/Demo real anchor controls disabled; wind lower in scroll. No intelligent drag claim.
Dark instrument cards display DEMO navigation/wind/depth with units and live state; scroll controls available; no bright primary surface.

Dark advisory-only SmartNav shows next course, course change, distance and estimated time, constant-SOG assumption and DEMO CPA timeline. Lower events accessible by scrolling; no autopilot command path.

physical_gates: Review, flash and verify C6 v2 expiry producer; compare GPS/heading/STW/wind/depth/rudder/motor/battery/tank/AIS values, references and instances; disconnect every sensor group while bridge stays live.
Configure and verify battery capacity/reserve/current sign/hotel loads; collect speed/power recordings, review/export/import empirical curve and compare predictions underway.

Bind actual pilot NAME/interface; verify read-only feedback before permission. In secured safe conditions test each of six manual commands separately, new feedback, rejection/timeout/reconnect, and physical STANDBY. No TRACK/WIND.
Validate actual target-PC touchscreen, DPI, GPU/OpenGL, chart catalog, plugin combinations and extended operation.
Supervised underway route progress, SmartNav/AIS advice, measured depth versus chart data, anchor alarms and energy; never treat advisory output as navigation certification.
limitations: Physical vessel, sensors, target PC, touchscreen and at-sea acceptance NOT RUN. Software commissioning release only; no navigation or production approval.
ESP32-C6 producer expiry patch compiled but not flashed. Older v1 mapping remains uncertain and cannot supply trusted advisory energy inputs.

Real pilot command transport supports only explicitly bound bidirectional TCP Actisense complete-PGN ASCII; physical PC/gateway/ESP32/SeaTalk/ST4000 path unaccepted. Every start/control reconnect is OFF. TRACK/WIND unavailable.
No accepted live ENC corridor provider or Pathfinder radar display/control adapter. Unavailable is explicit; no claim of safe water or collision avoidance.
Hosted Windows rejected hardware OpenGL; actual software fallback passed. Linux llvmpipe OpenGL passed. Target GPU, physical touch, broad chart/plugin catalogs remain open.
Diagnostic warning card still says ALPHA 1 / NOT FOR NAVIGATION above the correct Beta 1 version/commit. Cosmetic caption deferred, release identity verified independently.

At 150 percent the transient System popup partly covers the Alerts button; the critical text remains visible. Dismiss with Escape or an outside click before opening Alerts. Deferred presentation refinement.

At higher DPI or with alerts, the rail and long pages require Up/Down/pan scrolling. At 100 percent with an alert the lower heading card can be partly outside the viewport; users can prioritize speed in the configurable rail.
Native file pickers, installer and preserved Legacy/plugin dialogs can remain bright in Night. Primary XNav client surfaces passed dark-surface checks.

Unsigned Beta retains Alpha historical install directory, registry ownership and Start-menu folder for upgrade continuity. Installed modes share the normal profile; portable modes use an isolated profile.
Energy remains constant-condition advisory. Real capacity, current sign, hotel load, empirical curve and calibration need boat measurements. No hard-coded boat curve.
Recording replay does not move OpenCPN ownship or modify live route/AIS state. Default diagnostic export excludes navigation identifiers; selected recordings require explicit consent.
Pinned Signal K driver TLS/plain-WebSocket fallback policy is unchanged; trusted boat network only. External JSON bounds and malformed-input recovery are tested.
